rule: every row names a runnable checker or test and a planted mutant; a row without a passing checker cannot be PROVED; no novelty claim

obligations.statement: Task contract boundary: forbidden actions and actions above the task's authority are refused before any backend runs; a run with unauthorized attempts is never success; hidden protected state is read only by the checker.
obligations.checker: tests/m9/test_work.py; receipt unauthorized_attempts 0 for every arm

obligations.statement: Transfer contract: Λ(transported skill) = Λ(source) ⊗ Λ(correspondence); a missing role binding is ADAPTER_REQUIRED, a target operator whose registered role differs from the source role is REFUSE_TRANSFER (superficial similarity); revoking the correspondence or the source kills the transferred skill.

Skill induction is accepted only by the withheld intervention test (same distribution, unseen instances), never because the source episode succeeded; memoised, skeleton and subtrace inductions are compared.

Routing is a separate learning problem: the OCM router requires domain match, liveness, allowed actions, role agreement and no recorded failure; router error is measured separately from operator failure; brute-force 'try every skill' is the planted hostile.

Diagnosis targets the responsible layer (authority prevented, resource exhaustion, bad adapter, bad order, missing information, environment drift, wrong operator selected, operator wrong); revision under drift re-binds with lineage and ⊗ evidence; the old skill is never a timeless truth.

Lifetime transfer study on OCM-authored environments with exact oracle state: transfer matrix T0–T13 all as expected (14/14); transfer precision 6/6; later-domain acquisition cost 7 (transfer: one correspondence + one withheld run) vs 12 for matched parents that re-learn (fresh start with matched validation, trajectory memory, similarity skill library); success 54/54 for every arm; unauthorized attempts 0; paired success claims EQUIVALENT at n=9 (below the pre-registered minimum → CANNOT_CHECK for a SUPPORTED terminal).
